name: St. Padre Pio
title: Mystic, Stigmatist, Confessor
quote: Pray, hope, and don't worry. Worry is useless. God is merciful and will hear your prayer.

practices.d: Upon waking, immediately offer your day to God. 'Lord, I offer Thee all my prayers, works, joys, and sufferings of this day.'
Padre Pio's Mass was the centre of his life, often lasting two hours. Attend Mass daily if possible.
Spend thirty minutes in silent mental prayer before the Blessed Sacrament. Padre Pio spent hours in contemplation; even thirty minutes follows his spirit.
Padre Pio called it 'the weapon.' Pray at least five decades each day.
Read fifteen minutes from the Imitation of Christ, the lives of the saints, or St. John of the Cross.
Make a visit to the Blessed Sacrament during the day, even if brief. Padre Pio said that Jesus in the tabernacle waits for us with infinite patience and love.
Before sleep, examine your conscience honestly. Ask God to show you where you have failed in charity, patience, and faithfulness to your duties of state.
Before sleep, pray three Hail Marys for the grace of purity, invoking Our Lady's protection through the night.
Read from the lives of the saints or the Imitation of Christ, as Padre Pio recommended to his spiritual children.

penance: Offer up a physical suffering today without complaint, uniting it to the Passion of Christ.

prayers.title: Prayer After Holy Communion
prayers.latin: Mane nobiscum, Domine, quoniam advesperascit. Mane nobiscum, et esto nostra consolatio. Mane nobiscum, sol occasus nesciens.
prayers.eng: Stay with us, Lord, for evening is coming. Stay with us and be our consolation. Stay with us, O Sun that knows no setting.
prayers.note: Composed by St. Padre Pio, prayed after receiving Holy Communion.

prayers.title: Prayer for the Five Wounds
prayers.latin: O Domine Jesu Christe, qui sacratissimas manus et pedes tuos clavis affigi voluisti: concede mihi te totis viribus diligere, et in vulneribus tuis refugium et pacem invenire. Amen.
prayers.eng: O Lord Jesus Christ, Who didst submit to the nailing of Thy sacred hands and feet: grant me to love Thee with all my strength, and to find in Thy wounds my refuge and my peace. Amen.
prayers.note: Padre Pio bore the stigmata for 50 years.

name: St. Thérèse of Lisieux
title: Doctor of the Church · The Little Flower
quote: Miss no single opportunity of making some small sacrifice, here by a smiling look, there by a kindly word; always doing the smallest right, and doing it all for love.

practices.d: Offer your day as a 'little sacrifice of love' to Jesus. Aspire to please Him in every small thing.
Receive Holy Communion with total trust and childlike confidence.
Recall the mystery of the Incarnation three times a day; morning, noon, and evening.

practices.t: Do Small Things with Great Love
practices.d: Seek out tiny acts of kindness; a smiling look, a kind word, a cheerfully-borne inconvenience.
Receive every small annoyance as a gift from God. Never complain.
Make hidden sacrifices known only to God. Do not seek recognition.
Before sleep, abandon yourself into the merciful arms of Our Heavenly Father, as a little child.
Before bed, recall the small hidden sacrifices you offered throughout the day. Thank God for each one, no matter how small.
Pray before a crucifix or image of the Holy Face, offering reparation for sins against faith and the profanation of Sundays.

penance: Perform a small hidden sacrifice that no one will notice, offering it as a flower to Jesus.

prayers.title: Act of Oblation to Merciful Love
prayers.latin: O Deus meus, Sanctissima Trinitas, cupio te amare et te amari facere, ad gloriam sanctae Ecclesiae laborando, animas in terris salvando et eas quae in Purgatorio patiuntur liberando. Offero tibi omnia merita Sanctorum cum meis meritis et illis quae infinita bonitas tua in manus meas posuit. Amen.
prayers.eng: O my God, most Blessed Trinity, I desire to love Thee and to make Thee loved, to work for the glory of Holy Church by saving souls on earth and liberating those suffering in Purgatory. I offer Thee all the merits of the saints, with my own merits and those which Thy infinite goodness has placed in my hands. Amen.
prayers.note: St. Therese made this offering on June 9, 1895, the feast of the Most Holy Trinity.

prayers.title: Prayer of Confidence
prayers.latin: Deus meus, gratias tibi ago pro omnibus gratiis quas mihi concessisti, praesertim quod me per ignem tribulationis purificasti. In die novissimo te cum gaudio aspiciam, sceptrum Crucis ferens. Amen.
prayers.eng: My God, I thank Thee for all the graces Thou hast granted me, especially for having purified me in the crucible of suffering. I shall look upon Thee with joy at the last day, bearing the sceptre of the Cross. Since Thou didst deign to give me this precious Cross, I hope to resemble Thee in heaven and to see the sacred wounds of Thy Passion shine upon my glorified body. Amen.
prayers.note: From the last writings of St. Therese.

name: St. Thomas Aquinas
title: Doctor of the Church · Doctor Angelicus
quote: To one who has faith, no explanation is necessary. To one without faith, no explanation is possible.

practices.d: Pray: 'Creator of all things, true source of light and wisdom, deign to shed upon the darkness of my understanding the brightness of Thy light.'
Thomas celebrated Mass daily with profound reverence; he wept at the Consecration.
Silent meditation upon a single truth of faith. Simplicity is higher than complexity.
Read slowly from the Summa, Scripture, or the Church Fathers. Study is a form of prayer.
Thomas loved the Rosary for its simplicity; 'all the theology of the Incarnation in 50 beads.'
Make a visit to the Blessed Sacrament to adore Christ truly present. St. Thomas composed the Tantum Ergo and Adoro Te Devote; let his Eucharistic devotion inspire your own.
Pray the last hour of the Divine Office and retire in contemplative silence.
Ask: 'Did I think of God? Did my study lead me to love Him more?'

penance: Fast from unnecessary words today. Speak only what is true, necessary, and kind.

prayers.title: Prayer Before Study
prayers.latin: Creator ineffabilis, qui de thesauris sapientiae tuae tres Angelorum hierarchias designasti et eas super caelum empyreum miro ordine collocasti: concede mihi intelligentiam. Amen.
prayers.eng: O Creator beyond words, Who from the treasures of Thy wisdom didst appoint three hierarchies of Angels and set them in wonderful order above the heavens: grant me understanding. Amen.
prayers.note: St. Thomas prayed this before every study session.

prayers.title: Adoro Te Devote
prayers.latin:
Adóro te devóte, latens Déitas,
Quæ sub his figúris vere látitas:
Tibi se cor meum totum súbjicit,
Quia, te contémplans, totum déficit.

Visus, tactus, gustus in te fállitur,
Sed audítu solo tuto créditur:
Credo, quidquid dixit Dei Fílius,
Nil hoc verbo Veritátis vérius.

In Cruce latébat sola Déitas,
At hic latet simul et humánitas;
Ambo tamen credens atque cónfitens,
Peto, quod petívit latro pænitens.

Plagas, sicut Thomas, non intúeor,
Deum tamen meum te confíteor:
Fac me tibi semper magis crédere,
In te spem habére, te dilígere.

O memoriále mortis Dómini,
Panis vivus, vitam præstans hómini,
Præsta meæ menti de te vívere,
Et te illi semper dulce sápere.

Pie pellicáne, Jesu Dómine,
Me immúndum munda tuo Sánguine,
Cujus una stilla salvum fácere
Totum mundum quit ab omni scélere.

Jesu, quem velátum nunc aspício,
Oro, fiat illud, quod tam sítio:
Ut, te reveláta cernens fácie,
Visu sim beátus tuæ glóriæ.
Amen.
prayers.eng:
Godhead here in hiding, whom I do adore,
Masked by these bare shadows, shape and nothing more,
See, Lord, at thy service low lies here a heart
Lost, all lost in wonder at the God thou art.

Seeing, touching, tasting are in thee deceived:
How says trusty hearing? that shall be believed;
What God's Son has told me, take for truth I do;
Truth himself speaks truly or there's nothing true.

On the cross thy godhead made no sign to men,
Here thy very manhood steals from human ken:
Both are my confession, both are my belief,
And I pray the prayer of the dying thief.

I am not like Thomas, wounds I cannot see,
But can plainly call thee Lord and God as he;
Let me to a deeper faith daily nearer move,
Daily make me harder hope and dearer love.

O thou our reminder of Christ crucified,
Living Bread, the life of us for whom he died,
Lend this life to me then: feed and feast my mind,
There be thou the sweetness man was meant to find.

Bring the tender tale true of the Pelican;
Bathe me, Jesu Lord, in what thy bosom ran—
Blood whereof a single drop has power to win
All the world forgiveness of its world of sin.

Jesu, whom I look at shrouded here below,
I beseech thee send me what I thirst for so,
Some day to gaze on thee face to face in light
And be blest for ever with thy glory's sight.
Amen.
prayers.note: Composed by St. Thomas Aquinas for the feast of Corpus Christi. English translation by Gerard Manley Hopkins, S.J.

name: St. Benedict of Nursia
title: Father of Western Monasticism
quote: Ora et labora; Pray and work. Let nothing be preferred to the Work of God.

practices.d: Benedict's monks rose in the night for Vigils. Begin your day early, before the world demands your attention.
Pray the hour of Lauds from the Divine Office, greeting the new day with the Church's morning praise. If the full hour is not possible, pray at least one psalm.
Read Sacred Scripture slowly and prayerfully, lingering over words and phrases. Let the Word of God sink into your heart before beginning the day's labour.
Work with your hands or mind, but keep your heart fixed on God. Offer each task as a prayer.
Prime, Terce, Sext, None; short interruptions to remember God throughout the day.
Receive every person as Christ Himself. 'I was a stranger and you took me in.'
As the sun sets, pray Vespers to consecrate the evening hours to God. The Magnificat at Vespers is the great song of thanksgiving for the day's graces.
Eat your evening meal in silence or with spiritual reading, following the monastic custom of nourishing body and soul together at table.
End the day with Compline, the Church's night prayer. The Nunc Dimittis and final blessing place the night's rest under God's protection.

penance: Eat simply today: one full meal and two small collations, in the spirit of the Rule.

prayers.title: Prayer for a Happy Death
prayers.latin: O Domine Deus meus, ne tradas me in manus inimici: sed fac me victorem in hora mortis meae.
prayers.eng: O Lord my God, deliver me not into the hands of the enemy: but make me victorious in the hour of my death.
prayers.note: St. Benedict died standing, supported by his monks, arms raised in prayer.

prayers.title: The Medal Prayer
prayers.latin: Crux sacra sit mihi lux. Non draco sit mihi dux. Vade retro satana. Numquam suade mihi vana. Sunt mala quae libas. Ipse venena bibas.
prayers.eng: Let the Holy Cross be my light. Let not the dragon be my guide. Begone, Satan. Never tempt me with vanities. What you offer is evil. Drink your own poison.
prayers.note: Inscribed on the St. Benedict Medal, a powerful sacramental.

name: St. Teresa of Ávila
title: Doctor of the Church · Mystic, Reformer
quote: Let nothing disturb thee, nothing affright thee; all things are passing; God never changeth; patient endurance attaineth to all things; whoso God possesseth, in nothing is wanting; alone God sufficeth.

practices.d: Enter the 'interior castle'; turn within to the soul's centre, where Christ dwells.
Attend Holy Mass with interior recollection. As St. Teresa taught, the Mass is the greatest prayer; be fully present to the Sacred Mysteries.
Read from Teresa's Interior Castle, Way of Perfection, or Scripture.
Meditate on the mysteries. Teresa used the Rosary to steady her soul.
Throughout the day, withdraw briefly into the interior castle of your soul. Even amid work and conversation, maintain awareness of God's presence within you.
Accept every inconvenience with patient endurance; 'patience attains all things.'
Return again to the interior castle. Rest silently in God's presence.
Review the day's faults with humility. Trust in God's mercy.

penance: Deny yourself one comfort you normally enjoy, offering it for the conversion of sinners.

prayers.title: Bookmark Prayer
prayers.latin: Nihil te turbet, nihil te terreat. Omnia transeunt, Deus non mutatur. Patientia omnia obtinet. Qui Deum habet, nihil ei deest. Solus Deus sufficit.
prayers.eng: Let nothing disturb thee, nothing affright thee. All things are passing. God never changes. Patience attains all things. He who possesses God lacks nothing. God alone suffices.
prayers.note: Found in the breviary of St. Teresa after her death. Originally in Spanish.

prayers.title: Prayer of Self-Offering
prayers.latin: Tua sum, Domine. Pro te nata sum. Quid vis de me fieri? Sive dives sive pauper, sive gaudens sive dolens, sive consolata sive desolata: cum tu sis Rex meus, quid vis de me fieri? Loquere, Domine, quia audit serva tua. Amen.
prayers.eng: I am Thine, O Lord. I was born for Thee. What is Thy will for me? Let me be rich or beggared, exulting or repining, comforted or lonely. Since Thou art my King, what is Thy will for me? Speak, Lord, for Thy servant heareth. Amen.
prayers.note: From the writings of St. Teresa of Avila.

name: St. Josemaría Escrivá
title: Founder of Opus Dei
quote: Do everything for Love. Thus there will be no little things: everything will be big. Perseverance in the little things for Love is heroism.

practices.d: At the sound of the alarm, jump out of bed immediately. Consecrate the first minute of the day to Our Lord.
'Serviam'; I will serve. Offer the whole day to God through Mary.
The Mass is the centre and root of the interior life. Receive Communion daily.
Dedicate thirty minutes to silent mental prayer in the presence of the Blessed Sacrament or before a crucifix. Speak to God as a friend speaks to a friend.
Work well, for the love of God. Turn every task into prayer. This is Opus Dei; 'the Work of God.'
At noon, pause whatever you are doing and pray the Angelus. This brief interruption sanctifies the middle of the workday and honours the Incarnation.
Five decades daily. 'The Rosary is the most powerful weapon to conquer Satan.'
A brief visit in the midst of the day's work, even if only for a minute.
Read from a spiritual classic for at least fifteen minutes. St. Josemaria called this nourishment for the soul, as necessary as food for the body.
Examine yourself on one specific virtue you are working to acquire.

penance: Sanctify your ordinary work today by offering each task to God before beginning it.

prayers.title: Prayer for Sanctifying Work
prayers.latin: Domine, da mihi gratiam ut laborem meum ordinarium materiam sanctificationis meae videam. Adjuva me ut omne opus, omne colloquium, omne momentum hujus diei in orationem convertam, ut in fine diei totum tibi offerre possim tamquam aliquid amore tuo dignum. Amen.
prayers.eng: Lord, grant me the grace to see my ordinary work as the material for my sanctification. Help me to turn every task, every conversation, every moment of this day into a prayer, so that at its end I may offer it all to Thee as something worthy of Thy love. Amen.
prayers.note: Inspired by the spirit of Opus Dei, the sanctification of ordinary life.

prayers.title: Prayer to the Guardian Angels
prayers.latin: Sancti Angeli Custodes eorum qui meae curae commissi sunt: adjuvate me semper conscium esse Deum vigilare, et ei in illis fideliter et cum amore servire. Defendite me a maligno, et per vias pacis me ducite. Amen.
prayers.eng: Holy Guardian Angels of those in my care: help me always to be aware that God is watching, and to serve Him in them with fidelity and love. Defend me from the evil one, and lead me along the paths of peace. Amen.
prayers.note: St. Josemaria had a great devotion to the Guardian Angels.

name: St. Francis de Sales
title: Doctor of the Church · Bishop of Geneva
quote: Nothing is so strong as gentleness; nothing so gentle as real strength.

practices.d: Place yourself in God's presence. Foresee what the day will bring and resolve how to meet each thing with gentleness.
Unite yourself with Christ's Sacrifice. Receive Communion with sweet devotion.
A simple, affective meditation on a scene from the Gospels. Speak to Our Lord as a friend.
Gather 'little bouquets' of devout thoughts throughout the day. Return to them often.
Above all, be gentle; with others, with yourself, with circumstances. 'Nothing is so strong as gentleness.'
Francis loved the Rosary as a family prayer; slow, affectionate, meditative.
Review the day kindly. Thank God for graces, ask pardon for faults, resolve to amend.
Read from the Introduction to the Devout Life or the Treatise on the Love of God.

penance: Practice gentleness with everyone you meet today, especially those who irritate you.

prayers.title: Prayer of Gentle Trust
prayers.latin: Noli prospicere mutationes et casus hujus vitae cum timore; sed potius eas cum plena spe aspice, quia Deus, cujus es, te ex illis liberabit. Hucusque te custodivit; manum ejus tene, et per omnia te secure ducet. Amen.
prayers.eng: Do not look forward to the changes and chances of this life in fear; rather look to them with full hope that, as they arise, God, whose you are, will deliver you out of them. He has kept you hitherto; hold fast to His hand, and He will lead you safely through all things. Amen.
prayers.note: Adapted from the letters of St. Francis de Sales.

prayers.title: Prayer for a Devout Life
prayers.latin: Deus meus, totam voluntatem meam tibi dono. Hunc diem pro honore et gloria tua incipere desidero. Offero tibi omnes actiones hujus diei, et precor te ut mihi gratiam des nihil contra voluntatem tuam agendi. Illumina intellectum meum, robora voluntatem meam, purifica cor meum, et sanctifica animam meam. Amen.
prayers.eng: My God, I give Thee my whole will. I desire to begin this day for Thy honour and glory. I offer Thee all the actions of this day, and I pray Thee to give me the grace to do nothing that is contrary to Thy will. Enlighten my understanding, strengthen my will, purify my heart, and sanctify my soul. Amen.
prayers.note: Inspired by the Introduction to the Devout Life.
